messages:
Ben W: Heads-up — NVD just published CVE-2026-0451 affecting kms-client (<1.4.2). Potential key exposure during async rekey path. https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-0451

vuln-bot: Automated score: CVSS: 8.2/10 (High) | EPSS: 0.67 | Exploit: PoC repo (github.com/research/poc-kms-extract) | Affects: kms-client <1.4.2

Maria L: Confirmed via our SBOM: we depend on kms-client in private-deploy-agent and onprem-installer, pinned to 1.3.9 in service.yaml

Cain P: Attack vector looks local to app process memory (privilege required). For hosted Redwood API risk is lower; for Private/VPC customers who run on-prem it's higher — they often run with KMS credentials on the same host.

Natalie S: Assigning myself to coordinate patch + customer comms. Plan: upgrade to 1.4.2, run regression tests, schedule canary to dedicated infra, then roll to private deployments.

Ben W: Quick Q — any short-term workaround we can push to customers? Can we disable async rekey at runtime?

Maria L: Short term: yes — set KMS_REKEY_ASYNC=false in env for on-prem agents. Also recommend RBAC tweak: restrict kms-client service account to least privilege and rotate keys. Increase audit-log retention to 90d for affected tenants as a precaution.

Cain P: I'll open a fast-track PR to bump dependency in private-deploy-agent and add a feature flag to disable async rekey. PR: https://git.redwood/sr/private-deploy-agent/pulls/412

Natalie S: I'll draft an incident advisory for customers with private deployments. Suggested severity: HIGH. Mitigations: upgrade, apply env flag, tighten RBAC, enable enhanced auditing.

Ben W: For the triage board — set labels: vuln:high, component:kms, customer-impact:private-first. Also create follow-up to check SDK usage in Dedicated pools and hosted infra.

vuln-bot: Scan summary: 12 services flagged; 3 services running kms-client <1.4.2 in prod-dedicated, 4 in prod-private, 5 in staging. Full scan report: /scans/2026-03-15/1770012345

Maria L: ETA for patches: PRs opened, unit tests passing locally. Running e2e in staging tonight (US-west window). If green, canary tomorrow morning, full rollout within 48h.

Cain P: I'll add an audit-log hook to capture any rekey events and caller identity for backfill; will redact key material of course.

Natalie S: Logging guidance: record rekey events, caller identity, timestamp, but redact secrets. We'll include this in the customer advisory.

Ben W: Owners: Natalie (customer comms), Cain (patches/PRs), Maria (triage & rollout). I'll update the vuln tracker (VL-2026-1843). Please react :thumbsup: once added.

Maria L: Added to tracker and set due date 2026-03-18.

Natalie S: Draft notice sent to Legal for review. Will post customer-facing notice here when approved.

Ben W: Thanks everyone. If anyone spots active exploitation or noisy PoC hits, escalate to #incidents immediately and ping me.
